Hi all,

I dug into the pcap and logs. Short summary of what I’m seeing:
- Multiple outbound streaming connections from Pedestal show HTTP/2-style pseudo-headers (":path", ":method") arriving out-of-order relative to the header block.
- Our older connector parsing code (client SDK v2.2.x which Pedestal runs) assumes a stable header order when incrementally feeding frames into the streaming parser. Under certain TCP reordering conditions (seen in the pcap), the parser stalls waiting for a specific pseudo-header sequence and never emits the request to the runtime — this produces silent stalls and eventually 502/timeout.
- Server side (Redwood runtime) is not dropping tokens; the requests never fully reach the decode/executor layer because the parser state machine is blocked.

Mitigation options we can push now:
1) Pedestal: flip the SDK flag to enable lenient_header_mode (available behind a feature flag in v2.2.x) — this will allow the parser to accept reordered pseudo-headers. I’ll send the exact curl/config example in a follow-up.
2) If you can’t toggle config quickly, we can route a subset of traffic to a tolerant gateway pool (non-blocking parser) I can spin up from our side — this will be slightly higher latency but will restore throughput.
3) Short term: increase per-connection timeouts and enable connection retry/backoff on Pedestal side to reduce failed checkouts while we deploy a permanent SDK fix (v2.3.1).

Root cause (tentative): SDK parsing state machine makes a strict order assumption; network-level segment reordering exposes that. We should ship a parser fix (remove order assumption) and a defensive unit test that reorders header frames.

I’m marking this high priority. I’ll prepare a patch and a short validated build in the next 6–8 hours.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

Subject: Fix deployed to Pedestal — SDK patch + gateway workaround validated

Hi Natalie, Vanessa, and team —

Status update: we validated two actions this afternoon and the signals look good:

1) Gateway workaround — we routed 20% of Pedestal traffic to a tolerant gateway pool that uses a non-strict parser. Error rates dropped immediately on that slice (requests completing vs stalling).

2) SDK patch — we released v2.3.1 (parsed and unit-tested against reordered pseudo-header sequences) and Pedestal deployed the updated connector in their staging and then production canary. After the canary (10% traffic) we saw error rate fall to baseline and p99 latency return to ~130ms.

Next steps:
- I’ll open an MR with the parser unit tests and link INF-6243 to the MR.
- Vanessa/Rishi: coordinate the customer-facing exec one-pager and quantify the impact window for credits.
- We’ll run the postmortem next Tuesday and include remediation items (liberalize parser, add network reordering tests, and make lenient_header_mode default in client SDKs going forward).

Let me know if you want a quick walkthrough of the parser change — I can present in 30 minutes.

—Lauren
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
